title: Zigzag lights

clues.t: 26-year-old woman, sudden shimmering zigzag in her vision.
It spread slowly across one side over 20 minutes, then faded.
Then a throbbing headache on one side.
She vomited and had to lie in a dark room.
Her mother gets the same headaches.
Neurological examination is completely normal afterwards.

pearl: Aura builds gradually and fully reverses within an hour. Sudden aura that doesn’t build up, or comes with weakness, needs urgent review. Oestrogen-containing pills are usually avoided with aura.

title: Hot potato voice

clues.t: 15-year-old girl, sore throat and fever since yesterday.
It hurts to swallow, even her saliva.
No cough and no runny nose.
Swollen tender glands at the front of her neck.
Red tonsils with white pus on them.
Throat swab grows group A Streptococcus.

pearl: Fever, pus on the tonsils, tender neck glands and no cough together make strep more likely. Penicillin for 10 days in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander and other high-risk people helps prevent rheumatic fever.

title: Rolling over in bed

clues.t: 62-year-old woman, the room spins when she rolls onto her right side.
Each spin lasts under a minute.
Also when she looks up to a high shelf.
No hearing loss, no headache, no weakness.
Between episodes she feels fine.
Dix–Hallpike test to the right brings on vertigo and a twisting nystagmus.

pearl: Loose crystals in the inner ear’s canal cause it. The Epley manoeuvre fixes most cases in one or two goes. Tablets for dizziness don’t help and slow recovery.

title: Pain after the roast dinner

clues.t: 48-year-old woman, pain under her right ribs since last night.
It started an hour after a big fatty dinner.
Unlike her usual gallstone pains, it hasn’t gone away.
Fever 38.4 °C.
Pressing under her right ribs makes her stop breathing in.
Ultrasound: thick-walled gallbladder with stones and fluid around it.

pearl: Biliary colic settles within hours; cholecystitis doesn’t and comes with fever. Murphy’s sign is the catch on breathing in. Treatment: antibiotics and gallbladder removal, often in the same admission.

title: The eye that went grey

clues.t: 29-year-old woman, blurred vision in her left eye for 4 days.
It hurts to move the eye, and red looks washed out.
Two years ago, her right leg went numb for 3 weeks, then recovered.
Bending her neck sends a buzz down her back.
Hot showers make her symptoms flare briefly.
MRI: several white matter lesions near the ventricles, some enhancing.

pearl: Optic neuritis is a common first sign. Two episodes in different places at different times is the key pattern. Starting disease-modifying treatment early lowers relapses and disability.

title: Staring eyes, shaking hands

clues.t: 34-year-old woman, 6 kg weight loss despite eating more.
Heart racing, hands shaking, always too hot.
Her friends say she looks like she’s staring.
Her neck looks fuller, with a soft swelling that hums under the stethoscope.
TSH undetectable, free T4 very high.
TSH receptor antibodies positive.

pearl: The eye signs and the receptor antibodies separate it from other overactive thyroid causes. Smoking makes the eye disease much worse. Treatment options: carbimazole, radioactive iodine or surgery.

title: No pulse in her arm

clues.t: 24-year-old woman, months of tiredness, low fevers and weight loss.
Her left arm aches and goes pale when she hangs out washing.
The left radial pulse is weak.
Blood pressure: 135 in the right arm, 95 in the left.
A whooshing noise over her left collarbone.
PET-CT: inflamed, thickened aorta and left subclavian artery.

pearl: A vasculitis of the aorta and its branches, mostly in young women. Giant cell arteritis affects the same arteries but in people over 50. Treated with steroids and steroid-sparing drugs.

title: Every month, worse

clues.t: 22-year-old woman, period pain since her teens.
She misses university for 2 days every month.
The pain starts before bleeding and lasts after it.
Sex is painful deep inside.
Bowel motions hurt during her period.
Laparoscopy: dark spots and scarring on the pelvic lining.

pearl: About 1 in 7 Australian women. Period pain that stops you doing usual things isn’t normal. Today is International Women’s Day.

title: Burning and rushing

clues.t: 31-year-old woman, burning when she passes urine since this morning.
She’s rushing to the toilet every half hour.
Only a little comes out each time.
Lower tummy ache, no back pain.
No fever and no vaginal discharge.
Urine dipstick: nitrites and white cells positive.

pearl: Simple cystitis in a non-pregnant woman is treated with a short course of antibiotics. Fever, back pain or vomiting suggest a kidney infection, which needs prompt review.

title: Irregularly irregular
accept: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

clues.t: 72-year-old man, heart fluttering on and off for a week.
Breathless walking up the hill to the shops.
He drinks most nights and has high blood pressure.
His pulse is fast and completely irregular.
No P waves on the monitor.
ECG: irregularly irregular narrow complexes at 128 a minute.

pearl: The big risk is stroke. A CHA₂DS₂-VA score guides blood thinners. Rate or rhythm control helps symptoms. Alcohol, sleep apnoea and weight all matter.

title: Cola-coloured urine

clues.t: 8-year-old boy from a remote community.
His urine has turned dark brown, like cola.
Puffy eyes in the morning and swollen ankles.
Blood pressure is high for his age.
He had infected sores on his legs 3 weeks ago.
Low C3 complement; urine shows red cell casts.

pearl: It follows strep skin or throat infections. Most children recover fully. Treating skin sores and crowded housing are key in remote Australia. Today is World Kidney Day.

title: Collapsed at footy training

clues.t: 17-year-old boy fainted mid-sprint at football training.
He’s had chest tightness with hard exercise for months.
His uncle died suddenly at 35.
A murmur that gets louder when he stands up.
ECG: very tall voltages and deep T wave inversion.
Echo: septum 22 mm thick, blocking outflow on strain.

pearl: The most common inherited heart muscle disease, about 1 in 500. Fainting on exercise is a red flag. First-degree relatives need ECG and echo screening.

title: Tearing through to the back

clues.t: 58-year-old man, sudden severe chest pain while lifting.
He says it feels like tearing, going through to his back.
Long-standing poorly controlled blood pressure.
Blood pressure 170 in the right arm, 130 in the left.
A new early diastolic murmur.
CT angiogram: a flap in the ascending aorta.

pearl: Sudden, worst-ever pain that moves is the clue. Blood thinners for a presumed heart attack can be disastrous here. Ascending (type A) needs urgent surgery.

title: Burning in the sun

clues.t: 12-year-old boy, screams after 15 minutes in the sun.
Burning, stinging pain in his hands and face.
Hardly any rash, just mild swelling.
Sunscreen doesn’t help.
Window glass doesn’t protect him either.
Very high free protoporphyrin in red cells.

pearl: Visible light, not just UV, triggers it, so normal sunscreens fail. Children are often disbelieved because skin looks almost normal. Afamelanotide implants help some adults; liver monitoring is needed.

title: Numb at night

clues.t: 45-year-old woman, pins and needles in her right hand.
It wakes her at night; shaking the hand helps.
Thumb, index and middle fingers are affected.
Her little finger is fine.
Tapping over her wrist reproduces the tingling.
Nerve conduction: slowed median nerve at the wrist.

pearl: Common in pregnancy, diabetes and hypothyroidism. Night splints and steroid injection help many. Thumb muscle wasting means surgery shouldn’t wait.

title: Spring sneezes

clues.t: 19-year-old, sneezing fits every spring.
Runny nose with clear watery mucus.
Itchy eyes and itchy roof of the mouth.
Worse on windy days in the park.
No fever, feels otherwise well.
Skin prick test positive to ryegrass pollen.

pearl: A steroid nasal spray used every day works best. Hay fever is a risk factor for thunderstorm asthma, so people with spring hay fever should have a reliever plan.

title: Breathless after the flight

clues.t: 38-year-old woman, sudden breathlessness 2 days after a flight from London.
Sharp chest pain when she breathes in.
She takes the combined pill.
Heart rate 112, oxygen 92%.
Her right calf is swollen and tender.
CT pulmonary angiogram: clots in both lower lobe arteries.

pearl: Long travel, oestrogen and a swollen calf add up. Most are treated with blood thinners as an outpatient. A normal chest X-ray doesn’t rule it out.

title: Lopsided smile

clues.t: 41-year-old man, woke with his face drooping on the left.
He can’t close his left eye properly.
Drinks dribble from the corner of his mouth.
Ache behind his left ear yesterday.
He can’t wrinkle the left side of his forehead.
No weakness elsewhere; ears look normal.

pearl: Forehead involvement points to the nerve, not a stroke, where the forehead is spared. Prednisolone within 72 hours improves recovery. Tape the eye at night to protect it.

title: Worst headache of her life

clues.t: 44-year-old woman, sudden headache at the gym.
It hit its peak within seconds: the worst she’s ever had.
She vomited and her neck feels stiff.
She smokes and has high blood pressure.
She’s drowsy, but moves all four limbs.
CT brain: blood in the spaces around the brain.

pearl: Thunderclap onset is the key clue. CT within 6 hours is very sensitive; later, a lumbar puncture may be needed. Aneurysms are treated with coiling or clipping.

title: Stiff every morning

clues.t: 27-year-old man, low back pain for a year.
Worst in the morning, stiff for over an hour.
It gets better with exercise, not rest.
He wakes in the second half of the night with pain.
Last year he had a painful red eye that needed drops.
MRI: inflammation at both sacroiliac joints; HLA-B27 positive.

pearl: Inflammatory back pain improves with movement. Anti-inflammatories and exercise first; biologics if needed. Average delay to diagnosis is years, so ask about morning stiffness.

title: Deafness in the family

clues.t: 19-year-old man, blood in his urine on a routine check.
He’s worn hearing aids since he was 14.
His maternal uncle had a kidney transplant at 30.
His urine also shows protein.
Eye check: a cone-shaped bulge of the lens.
Gene test: COL4A5 variant.

pearl: A collagen fault in the kidneys, ears and eyes. The X-linked form is most severe in males. Starting ACE inhibitors early slows kidney decline.

title: First steps hurt

clues.t: 50-year-old man, sharp heel pain for 2 months.
Worst with his first steps in the morning.
Eases after walking a bit, then aches by evening.
He recently took up running on the road.
Tender spot on the inside of the heel underneath.
No swelling, numbness or redness.

pearl: Calf and foot stretches, supportive shoes and load changes work for most within a year. Heel spurs on X-ray are common and don’t cause the pain.

title: Itchy elbows

clues.t: 7-year-old girl, itchy rash for years that comes and goes.
It’s in the creases of her elbows and behind her knees.
The skin is dry, red and thickened from scratching.
Worse in winter and after hot baths.
She has asthma and hay fever.
Her dad had the same as a child.

pearl: Daily moisturiser and a steroid cream for flares are the mainstays. Steroid creams used properly are safe. Weeping or crusted patches may be infected.

title: Three months of coughing

clues.t: 36-year-old man, cough for 3 months.
Night sweats soak his sheets; he’s lost 7 kg.
He moved to Australia from Papua New Guinea last year.
Last week he coughed up some blood.
Chest X-ray: a cavity in the right upper lobe.
Sputum: acid-fast bacilli, PCR positive for M. tuberculosis.

pearl: TB is curable with 6 months of combined antibiotics. Contacts are tested. Australia has one of the lowest rates in the world, but it’s common next door. Today is World TB Day.

title: Irregular and spotty

clues.t: 24-year-old woman, periods only 4 times a year.
Hair growing on her chin and tummy.
Acne that started late in her teens.
Her weight has crept up and she’s struggling to lose it.
Free testosterone mildly raised; prolactin and thyroid normal.
Ultrasound: many small follicles in both ovaries.

pearl: Two of three needed: irregular cycles, high androgens (blood or signs), polycystic ovaries. It raises the risk of diabetes, so check glucose. The pill, metformin and lifestyle all help.

title: Déjà vu, then nothing

clues.t: 33-year-old woman, episodes her husband calls ‘zoning out’.
Each starts with a rising feeling in her stomach and strong déjà vu.
Then she stares and smacks her lips for a minute.
She doesn’t remember it and is confused afterwards.
She had long seizures with fevers as a toddler.
MRI: hippocampal sclerosis on the left.

pearl: The most common focal epilepsy in adults. If tablets fail, surgery can make many people seizure-free. Today is Purple Day for epilepsy awareness.

title: Itch without a rash

clues.t: 54-year-old woman, maddening itch for a year, worst at night.
No rash, just scratch marks.
Tired all the time.
Dry eyes and mouth.
ALP very high, bilirubin normal.
Anti-mitochondrial antibodies strongly positive.

pearl: An autoimmune condition of the small bile ducts, mostly in middle-aged women. Ursodeoxycholic acid slows progression. Check bone density: osteoporosis is common.

title: Frozen in fright

clues.t: 46-year-old woman, back and legs increasingly rigid for a year.
A sudden noise makes her whole body spasm and she falls stiff like a statue.
She’s afraid to cross roads and walks with a wide, careful gait.
She has type 1 diabetes.
EMG: continuous muscle firing at rest.
Very high anti-GAD antibodies.

pearl: Often mistaken for anxiety at first. Diazepam and baclofen ease the stiffness; immune treatments help some. Its link with type 1 diabetes comes from the shared GAD antibody.

title: The seal bark

clues.t: 2-year-old boy, a cold for 2 days.
Tonight he woke with a barking cough like a seal.
A harsh noise when breathing in while he cries.
Mild fever, still drinking.
Settles when calm on mum’s lap.
Ages 6 months to 3 years is the peak.

pearl: A single dose of oral steroid helps most children. Noise at rest, drooling or blue lips need an ambulance. Keep the child calm; steam doesn’t help.

title: No sleep needed

clues.t: 23-year-old man, barely slept for 5 nights but full of energy.
Talking fast, jumping from idea to idea.
Spent his savings on a business plan in one night.
Feels he has a special mission.
Last year he had months of deep depression.
No drugs found on a urine screen.

pearl: Mania plus past depression is the pattern. Antidepressants alone can trigger mania, so the diagnosis matters. Lithium and other mood stabilisers prevent relapse. Today is World Bipolar Day.

title: Thirsty, then breathless

clues.t: 16-year-old girl, very thirsty and passing lots of urine for 3 weeks.
Lost 5 kg without trying.
Today vomiting and tummy pain.
Deep, sighing breaths and a fruity smell on her breath.
Blood glucose 28 mmol/L, ketones 5.2.
Venous pH 7.12.

pearl: Often the first sign of type 1 diabetes. Thirst, weight loss and passing lots of urine in a young person needs a same-day finger-prick glucose. Treated with fluids, insulin and potassium.
